The test image shows a soybean stem/root near the soil line with reddish-brown to orange-brown discoloration and some dark lesions. This appears to be a root/stem rot disease. Top candidates: Phytophthora, Fusarium, Rhizoctonia, Pythium_damping_off.

Let me view reference images for these candidates in parallel.

The Rhizoctonia reference image (bottom-left panel) shows a very similar pattern to the test image — a hand holding a stem near soil with reddish-brown/orange discoloration. Let me view more candidates to confirm.
The Rhizoctonia reference (bottom-left) is a near-identical match to the test image. Let me view more references to meet the minimum requirement.

**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image features:**
- Soybean stem/hypocotyl held near soil line
- Reddish-brown to orange-brown external discoloration on lower stem
- Dark lesion spot visible
- Appears to be near-soil rot at early-to-mid season

**Key comparison findings:**
- **Rhizoctonia**: The bottom-left panel of the Rhizoctonia reference collage is nearly identical to the test image — same hand-holding-stem-near-dark-soil composition, same reddish-brown/orange external lesion pattern on the lower stem. This is an exceptionally strong visual match.
- **Phytophthora**: Dark chocolate-brown discoloration typically extending up multiple nodes; different color tone and pattern.
- **Fusarium**: Deep internal brown vascular rot; different from the external lesion visible in the test.
- **Pythium**: Early seedling water-soaked lesions; different stage and appearance.
- All leaf/pod diseases (Bacterial_Blight, Cercospora, Frogeye, Septoria, etc.) are clearly not applicable — wrong plant part entirely.

The reddish-brown sunken lesion on the lower stem/hypocotyl near the soil line is the hallmark of **Rhizoctonia** root and stem rot, and the reference collage confirms this with a nearly identical photograph.
